"Regarding things external, regarding things internal,
how can one arrive at a measure of nobility and baseness? How can one arrive at a measure of smallness and greatness?"
Běihǎi Ruò (北海若), the God of the Northern Sea, said:
"Viewing it from the perspective of the Dao,
things have no nobility or baseness;
viewing it from the perspective of things,
they consider themselves noble and each other base;
viewing it from the perspective of custom,
nobility and baseness do not reside in oneself.
Viewing it from the perspective of difference,
according to that which they are large, enlarge them,
then all things are not large;
according to that which they are small, make them small,
then all things are not small;
knowing that Heaven and Earth are like a grain of rice,
knowing that a downy hair is like a hill or mountain,
then the differences in number will be seen.
Viewing it from the perspective of function,
according to that which they possess, give them possession,
then all things possess;
Because of its non-existence, make it non-existent;
then all things will be without exception non-existent.
Knowing that east and west are opposite but cannot do without each other,
then the division of labor is fixed.
From the viewpoint of inclination,
because of what it is, affirm it;
then all things will be without exception affirmed.
Because of what it is not, deny it;
then all things will be without exception denied.
Knowing that Yáo and Jié are naturally opposed to each other,
then the direction of inclination is seen.
"In the past, Yáo and Shùn yielded and became emperors,
Zǐ Kuài yielded and was overthrown;
Tāng and Wǔ contended and became kings,
Bái Gōng contended and was destroyed.
From this perspective,
the rites of contention and yielding,
the actions of Yáo and Jié,
nobility and lowliness have their times,
and cannot be taken as constant.
A liáng lì (a type of battering ram) can breach a city wall,
but cannot block a hole;
this speaks of different tools.
Qíjì and Huáliú,
in one day can gallop a thousand miles,
but are not as good as a lìshēng (wildcat) at catching mice;
this speaks of different skills.
An owl catches fleas at night
and discerns the finest hairs.
But when it emerges in daylight, it glares
and cannot see hills and mountains.
This shows that their natures are different.
Thus it is said:
"Is it possible to take only a teacher of correctness and have no error,
only a teacher of order and have no chaos?"
This shows a lack of understanding of the principles of Heaven and Earth,
and the true nature of all things.
This is like taking only Heaven as a teacher and not Earth,
or only *yīn* as a teacher and not *yáng*.
That this is unworkable is clear.
Yet they continue to speak without ceasing,
which is either foolish or deceitful.
Emperors and kings have different abdication rituals;
the Three Dynasties had different systems of succession.
To act contrary to the times
and go against the customs
is called the act of an usurper;
to act in accordance with the times
and follow the customs
is called the way of righteousness.
Be silent, Hébó!
How could you know the gates of nobility and baseness,
the affairs of the small and the great!"
Hébó said: "Then what should I do,
and what should I not do?
"My acceptance and rejection, my inclination and abandonment,
what can I ultimately do?"
Běihǎi Ruò said:
"Viewing it from the perspective of the Dao,
what is noble, what is base?
This is called reversion and expansion.
If you are constrained in your aspirations,
you will be greatly obstructed from the Dao.
What is little, what is much?
This is called discarding and bestowing.
If you act with only one thing in mind,
you will diverge from the Dao.
Dignified, as if a country has its ruler,
yet he has no personal virtue;
unrestrained, as if a sacrifice has its earth altar,
yet it brings no private blessings;
drifting, as if the four directions are without limit,
without any boundaries.
Embracing all things,
who bears its wings?
This is called without direction.
All things are equal,
who is short, who is long?
The Dao has no beginning or end,
things have death and life,
do not rely on their completion;
one emptiness, one fullness,
do not locate them according to their form.
Years cannot be grasped,
time cannot be stopped;
waxing and waning, fullness and emptiness,
when something ends, it has a beginning.
This is the way to speak of the grand principles,
and to discuss the reasons for all things.
The creation of things
is like a sudden rush or a gallop,
there is no movement without change,
and no moment without alteration.
What should one do,
and what should one not do?
For things are surely transforming themselves!"
The Hé Bo (河伯), the God of the Yellow River, said: "Then what is valuable about the Dao?"
Běi Hǎi Ruò (北海若), the God of the Northern Sea, said:
"One who knows the Dao must be versed in principle;
one who is versed in principle must be clear about expediency;
one who is clear about expediency
will not harm himself with things.
One with supreme virtue
cannot be heated by fire,
cannot be drowned by water,
cannot be harmed by cold or heat,
and cannot be injured by birds or beasts.
It is not to say that they are contemptuous of these things,
but rather that they discern safety and danger,
are at peace with misfortune and fortune,
are cautious in departing and approaching,
And nothing can harm it.
Therefore, it is said:
"Heaven is within,
man is without,
virtue lies in Heaven."
Knowing that the actions of a great man
are rooted in Heaven
and positioned in virtue;
he hesitates and stretches,
returning to the essential and speaking of the ultimate."
Someone asked, "What is meant by Heaven,
what is meant by man?"
Běihǎi Ruò 北海若 said:
"Cattle and horses having four legs
is called Heaven;
hobbling the horse's head,
piercing the ox's nose,
is called man.
Therefore, it is said:
Do not use man to extinguish Heaven,
do not use artifice to extinguish fate,
do not use virtue to sacrifice reputation.
Carefully guard it and do not lose it,
this is called returning to its true nature."
The Kuí 夔 pities the xián 蚿,
the xián 蚿 pities the snake,
the snake pities the wind,
the wind pities the eye,
Eyes envy the heart.
Kuí said to the xián:
"I hop along on one foot,
and no one can compare to me.
Now, you make use of ten thousand feet; how do you do it?"
The xián said:
"Not so.
Have you not seen a spitter?
When he spits, the larger drops are like pearls,
the smaller like mist,
and the mixed ones that fall are countless.
Now, I move my natural mechanism,
but I do not know why it is so."
The xián said to the snake:
"I walk with many feet,
but I cannot match your footlessness;
why is that?"
The snake said:
"The movements of the natural mechanism,
how can they be changed?
What use do I have for feet?"
The snake said to the wind:
"I move my spine and ribs to travel,
and there is a similarity.
Now you, rising vigorously from the North Sea,
vigorously enter the South Sea,
and yet seem to be nothing;
why is that?"
Fēng (風) said:
"Indeed.
I rise boisterously from the Běi Hǎi (北海)
and enter the Nán Hǎi (南海).
Yet, pointing at me will defeat me,
flicking at me with a finger will also defeat me.
However,
the one who can break large trees
and blow away large houses
is only me.
Therefore, using many small (defeats) to achieve
a great victory is the idea.
Achieving great victory
is something only a sage can do."
Kǒng Zǐ (孔子) was traveling in Kuāng (匡) when
the people of Sòng (宋) surrounded him several times over,
yet he continued playing his lute and singing without cease.
Zǐ Lù (子路) entered to see him,
and said:
"Why is the Master so merry?"
Kǒng Zǐ (孔子) said:
"Come!
I will tell you.
I have avoided poverty for a long time
and yet could not escape it; it is fate.
I have sought understanding for a long time
and have not obtained it; it is the times.
When Yáo (堯) and Shùn (舜) were in power, there were no poor people in the world,
It's not that they knew how to gain it;
when Jié 桀 and Zhòu 紂 reigned,
the world had no wise men,
it's not that they knew how to lose it;
it was simply the circumstances of the time.
Now, for one who travels on the water and does not avoid jiāolóng 蛟龍 (mythical aquatic dragons),
that is the bravery of a fisherman;
for one who travels on land and does not avoid sìhǔ 兕虎 (rhinoceros and tiger),
that is the bravery of a hunter;
for one who faces the clash of swords
and regards death as if it were life,
that is the bravery of a staunch warrior;
for one who knows that misfortune is destined,
who knows that success comes at the right time,
and who is not afraid when facing great difficulties,
that is the bravery of a sage.
It depends on where you are;
my fate is controlled by something."
Before long,
the armor-clad general advanced,
and said his explanation:
"We thought it was Yáng Hǔ 陽虎,
therefore we surrounded him.
Now that it is not,
please allow us to withdraw and retire."
Gōngsūn Lóng 公孫龍 asked Wèi Mù 魏牟, saying:
"I, Lóng 龍, learned the ways of the former kings when I was young,
and as I grew older, I came to understand the practices of benevolence and righteousness;
Identifying agreement and difference,
Separating hardness and whiteness;
Affirming the un-affirmable,
Accepting the un-acceptable;
Confusing the wisdom of a hundred schools,
Exhausting the eloquence of countless mouths;
I considered myself supremely knowledgeable.
Now I hear Zhuāngzǐ’s words,
And am utterly perplexed by them.
I don't know if my arguments are inadequate,
Or my knowledge is inferior.
Now I have nowhere to open my beak,
I dare to ask for the method."
Gōngzǐ Mù leaned on his armrest, sighed deeply,
Looked up to the sky and laughed, saying:
"Have you not heard of the frog in the collapsed well?
It said to the turtle of the Eastern Sea:
'How joyful I am!
I leap and frolic on the well's edge,
And rest in the crannies of the broken bricks;
When I rush into the water, I support my armpits and hold up my chin,
When I kick in the mud, my feet are submerged and my toes disappear;
Furthermore, the water striders, crabs, and tadpoles,
None can compare to me.
Moreover, possessing all the water in a single gully, and straddling the joy of this collapsed well,
This is indeed the ultimate!
Why doesn't master come and observe it regularly!'
Before the Eastern Sea turtle's left foot had entered,
And his right knee was already tied.
Thereupon he hesitated and retreated,
and told him,
"The sea, a thousand *lǐ* in distance,
is not enough to encompass its vastness;
a thousand *rèn* in height,
is not enough to fathom its depth.
In the time of Yǔ
for ten years there were nine floods, but the water did not increase or add to it;
in the time of Tāng
for eight years there were seven droughts, but the cliffs did not increase or diminish.
That which does not change due to short or long periods,
and does not advance or retreat due to more or less,
this is also the great joy of the East Sea."
Thereupon, the frog in the dilapidated well heard this,
and was nervously startled,
and filled with anxious self-doubt.
"Furthermore, to not know the boundary of right and wrong,
and yet still desire to observe the words of Zhuāngzǐ,
is like making a mosquito carry a mountain,
or a *shāngjù* snail race across the river;
it certainly will not be up to the task.
Moreover, to not know the ultimately wondrous words,
and to be content with temporary benefits,
are they not just frogs in a dilapidated well?
Furthermore, he is one who treads the Yellow Springs
and ascends to the Great Void,
Neither south nor north,
it bursts open and disperses in all four directions,
sinking into the unfathomable;
neither east nor west,
it begins in the mysterious darkness,
and returns to the great thoroughfare.
You, however, meticulously seek it with scrutiny,
and search for it with argument.
This is simply using a pipe to peep at the sky,
and using an awl to point at the earth;
is it not small indeed!
Go away!
Moreover, have you not heard of the Shòulíng yúzi (壽陵餘子) learning to walk in Hándān (邯鄲)?
Not having acquired the skills of that state,
they also lost their original way of walking,
and simply crawled back home.
If you do not leave now,
you will forget your original self,
and lose your profession."
Gōngsūn Lóng's (公孫龍) mouth opened but would not close,
his tongue raised but would not descend,
and then he fled.
Zhuāngzǐ (莊子) was fishing in the Pú River (濮水),
when the king of Chǔ (楚) sent two senior officials to announce to him,
saying,
"I wish to trouble you with the administration of my kingdom!"
Zhuāngzǐ (莊子), holding his fishing rod without turning his head, said,
Said:
"I have heard that Chǔ had a divine tortoise,
dead for three thousand years already.
The king wrapped it in cloth and stored it in a chest atop the ancestral hall.
This tortoise,
would it rather be dead, leaving its bones to be valued,
or would it rather be alive, dragging its tail in the mud?"
The two high officials said:
"Rather be alive and drag its tail in the mud."
Zhuāngzǐ said:
"Be gone!
I shall drag my tail in the mud."
Huìzi was the prime minister of Liáng.
Zhuāngzǐ went to see him.
Someone said to Huìzi:
"Zhuāngzǐ has come,
wanting to replace you as prime minister."
Thereupon Huìzi became afraid
and searched throughout the kingdom for three days and three nights.
Zhuāngzǐ went to see him,
and said:
"In the south there is a bird,
its name is yuānchú
do you know of it?
This yuānchú, it sets out from the South Sea
and flies to the North Sea.
It will not perch except on the wútóng tree,
it will not eat except liànshí fruit,
He would not drink unless it was sweet spring water.
Thereupon a kite obtained a rotten rat,
a yuānchú (鵷鶵) bird passed by,
looked up at it and said:
"Shoo!"
Now, do you want to use your Liáng (梁) kingdom
to frighten me?"
Zhuāngzǐ (莊子) was strolling with Huìzǐ (惠子) on the bridge over the Háo (濠) River.
Zhuāngzǐ (莊子) said:
"The shū (儵) fish come out and swim freely,
this is the fish's happiness."
Huìzǐ (惠子) said:
"You are not a fish,
how do you know the fish's happiness?"
Zhuāngzǐ (莊子) said:
"You are not me,
how do you know that I do not know the fish's happiness?"
Huìzǐ (惠子) said:
"I am not you,
so I certainly do not know you;
you certainly are not a fish either,
so you do not know the fish's happiness, that is complete."
Zhuāngzǐ (莊子) said:
"Let's please go back to the beginning.
When you said,
'How do you know the fish's happiness?',
you already knew that I knew it when you asked me.
I know it on the Háo (濠) River above."
Chapter 18: Supreme Joy
Does the world possess supreme joy?
Is there a way to preserve life?
What should we do and what should we rely on now?
What should we avoid and where should we dwell?
What should we pursue and what should we abandon?
What should we delight in and what should we detest?
Now, what the world values are
wealth, nobility, longevity, and goodness.
What they delight in are
bodily comfort, rich flavors, beautiful clothes, attractive women, and pleasing sounds.
What they look down upon are
poverty, lowliness, early death, and wickedness.
What they suffer from are
the body not obtaining comfort and ease,
the mouth not obtaining rich flavors,
the form not obtaining beautiful clothes,
the eyes not obtaining attractive women,
the ears not obtaining pleasing sounds.
If one does not obtain these,
then one is greatly worried and fearful.
Their actions for the body are truly foolish!
The wealthy person
toils hard and works diligently,
accumulating much wealth but not being able to fully use it.
Their actions for the body are truly external.
The noble person
Working night and day,
contemplating good and bad,
his body is also becoming emaciated.
A person's life,
is born with worries.
The long-lived are muddled;
prolonged worry without death,
what bitterness is this!
His body is also becoming estranged.
Distinguished scholars are considered good by the world,
but this is not enough to preserve their own lives.
I do not know whether what is considered good is truly good, or truly not good.
If it is considered good,
it is insufficient to preserve life;
if it is considered not good,
it is sufficient to keep people alive.
Therefore it is said:
"If loyal advice is not heeded,
crouch down and do not contend."
Thus, Fū Zǐxū 夫子胥 contended and harmed his body;
if he had not contended,
his name would not have been made.
Is there truly good or not?
Now, what common people do and what they enjoy,
I do not know whether enjoyment is truly enjoyment,
or truly not enjoyment.
I observe what the common people enjoy,
when they all rush to it,
Restrained and forced, as if there were no choice,
and all of them saying it is joyful,
I do not find it joyful,
nor do I find it not joyful.
Is there truly joy or not?
I consider non-action to be true joy,
and yet the common people consider it the greatest suffering.
Therefore, it is said:
"Ultimate joy is no joy,
ultimate praise is no praise."
The rights and wrongs of the world are truly not yet settled.
However,
non-action can settle rights and wrongs.
Ultimate joy preserves the body,
only through non-action can one nearly survive.
Please allow me to try to explain it.
Heaven is clear because of non-action,
the earth is tranquil because of non-action,
therefore when the two non-actions combine,
all things are transformed and born.
Vague and obscure,
yet from where does it come forth!
Obscure and vague,
yet it has no form!
The myriad things bustling,
all propagate from non-action.
Therefore, it is said:
Heaven and earth practice non-action,
and nothing is not done.
As a human, who can attain non-action?
When Zhuāng Zǐ's 莊子 wife died,
Huìzǐ 惠子 went to offer condolences.
Zhuāng Zǐ 莊子 was squatting with his legs spread apart, drumming on a basin and singing.
Huìzǐ 惠子 said, "Living with someone, growing old together until death,
not crying would be enough.
But you're drumming on a basin and singing,
isn't that going too far!"
Zhuāng Zǐ 莊子 said:
"Not so.
When she had just died,
how could I alone be without some grief?
But considering her beginning, she fundamentally had no life.
Not only had no life,
but fundamentally had no form.
Not only had no form,
but fundamentally had no breath.
Mingling within the vast obscurity,
it transformed and there was breath.
Breath transformed and there was form.
Form transformed and there was life.
Now it transforms again and goes to death.
This is like the four seasons of spring, autumn, winter, and summer following each other.
If someone is peacefully sleeping in a great house,
and I am wailing and crying following after her,
I would think of myself as not understanding fate.
Therefore, I stopped."
Zhīlí Shū and Huájiè Shū were observing at the mound of Míngbó,
the void of Kūnlún,
the place where the Yellow Emperor, Huángdì, rested.
Suddenly, a willow tree grew from his left elbow,
and his mind was perturbed and disgusted by it.
Zhīlí Shū said, "Do you dislike it?"
Huájiè Shū said, "No, why should I dislike it!
Life is a temporary loan;
that which is lent and gives rise to life,
is but dust and grime.
Life and death are like day and night.
Moreover, you and I are observing transformation,
and the transformation has reached me,
so why should I dislike it!"
Zhuāng Zǐ went to Chǔ,
and saw an empty skull,
clearly showing its form.
He tapped it with his horse whip,
and thereupon questioned it,
saying:
"Sir, did you, greedy for life, lose reason,
and thus come to this?
Or did you have affairs of a vanquished state,
and suffer the punishment of the axe,
and thus come to this?
Or did you have immoral conduct,
ashamed to leave behind the disgrace of your parents, wife, and children,
and thus come to this?
Are you doing this because you fear your children will suffer from cold and hunger?
Or
is it that your years
have truly reached this point?"
Having finished speaking,
he picked up the skull,
and used it as a pillow to sleep.
In the middle of the night,
the skull appeared in his dream and said:
"You who speak seem to be a debater.
All that you gentlemen say
are burdens of the living;
in death, there are none of these.
Do you wish to hear about death?"
Zhuāngzǐ said: "Yes."
The skull said:
"In death,
there is no ruler above,
no subject below;
there are also no affairs of the four seasons.
Freely taking Heaven and Earth as spring and autumn,
even the joy of a king ruling from the south
cannot surpass it."
Zhuāngzǐ did not believe it,
and said:
"I will have the Simìng
restore your form,
make flesh and muscle on your bones,
To betray one's parents, wife, neighbors, and acquaintances,
is that what you desire?"
The skull deeply frowned, wrinkling its nose, and said:
"How could I possibly abandon the joy of facing south as a king
and return to the toil of the human world!"
Yán Yuān went east to Qí,
and Confucius had a worried expression.
Zǐ Gòng descended from his mat and asked:
"I, a junior, dare to ask,
since Huí is going east to Qí, why does the Master have a worried expression?"
Confucius said: "Excellent question!
In the past, Guǎn Zǐ had a saying,
which I greatly appreciate,
saying:
'A small pouch cannot hold a large object,
and a short rope cannot draw from a deep well.'
Those who are like this
believe that their destiny is fixed
and their form is predetermined;
they cannot be diminished or increased.
I fear that Huí will speak to the Marquis of Qí
about the Way of Yáo, Shùn, and the Yellow Emperor,
and further burden him with the words of Suìrén
and Shénnóng.
He will then seek inwardly within himself
and not find it;
if he does not find it, he will be confused,
and when people are confused, they die.
Moreover, have you alone not heard?
In the past, a seabird landed in the suburbs of Lǔ;
the Marquis of Lǔ welcomed it and feasted it in the temple,
performed the *Jiǔsháo* music for its pleasure,
and prepared a full offering of livestock for its meal.
The bird then became dizzy and gazed around, sad and mournful,
All enter into the mechanism.
Chapter 19: *Dáshēng* (Attaining Life)
Those who understand the nature of attaining life
do not strive for what life cannot do without.
Those who understand the nature of attaining destiny
do not strive for what knowledge can do nothing about.
Nourishing the body must begin with things.
There are those who have a surplus of things, yet their bodies are not nourished.
Having life must begin with not being separated from the body.
There are those whose bodies are not separated, yet their lives perish.
The coming of life cannot be rejected;
its departure cannot be stopped.
Alas!
The people of the world think that nourishing the body is sufficient to preserve life.
But if nourishing the body is truly insufficient to preserve life,
then what is the world worth?
Although it is not worth
doing, yet cannot be avoided,
the doing cannot be escaped.
Now, if one wishes to be spared from toiling for the body,
there is nothing better than abandoning the world.
Abandoning the world results in no encumbrances;
with no encumbrances, one is upright and balanced;
being upright and balanced, one regenerates with that other (the Dao);
regenerating with that other, one is near perfection.
What affair is worth abandoning, and what life is worth leaving behind?
Abandoning affairs means the body is not strained;
leaving behind life means the essence is not depleted.
When the body is whole and the essence is restored,
one becomes one with Heaven.
Heaven and earth are the parents of all things;
united, they form a body;
dispersed, they become a beginning.
How can things be brought to a halt!
He will dwell in the measure of non-excess,
and be hidden in the discipline of no beginning,
roam in the place where the myriad things end and begin,
unify his nature,
nourish his qi,
harmonize his virtue,
in order to connect with that by which things are made.
Now, if someone is like this,
his heaven-given nature is completely preserved,
his spirit has no flaw,
from where would things enter him!
"Now, one who is drunk and falls from a carriage,
though the fall is swift, does not die.
His bones and joints are the same as other people's,
but the harm he suffers is different from other people's.
His spirit is complete.
When he rides, he does not know it;
when he falls, he does not know it.
Death, life, alarm and fear do not enter his breast,
therefore, he confronts objects without being frightened.
He obtains completeness from wine and is still like this,
how much more so if he obtains completeness from Heaven?
The sage is hidden in Heaven,
therefore, nothing can harm him.
A revenger does not break the Mó gān (鏌干 sword),
even one with a resentful heart does not blame a flying tile,
therefore, the world is equable.
Therefore, there is no chaos of attack and war,
and there are no executions involving killing,
because of this Way.
Do not open the Heaven of people,
but open the Heaven of Heaven.
One who opens the Heaven of Heaven, virtue is born,
Among the myriad things,
he is solely focused on the cicada's wings.
"I neither turn nor tilt,
I would not exchange the cicada's wings for all the world.
What would I do and not succeed!"
Kǒngzǐ turned and said to his disciples,
"When the will is undivided,
it becomes concentrated in the spirit.
Is this not what is meant by the hunchbacked old man!"
Yán Yuān asked Zhòngní,
"I once crossed the deep Shāngshēn Abyss,
and the ferryman's handling of the boat was like that of a spirit.
I asked him,
saying,
'Can boat handling be learned?'
He said,
'Yes.
Those who are good swimmers can do it with practice.
But as for those who dive,
they have never seen a boat
and yet can handle it easily.'
I asked him, but he did not tell me the answer.
I venture to ask, what does he mean?"
Zhòngní said,
"Those who are good swimmers can do it with practice,
because they forget the water.
As for those who dive
who have never seen a boat
and thus easily controlled by him.
He views deep pools as hills,
and the overturning of boats as merely the backing up of his own carriage.
The myriad overturnings and backings are displayed before him,
yet he cannot even enter his house.
Where could he go and not be pressed for time!
When betting with roof tiles, one is skillful;
when betting with belt hooks, one is apprehensive;
when betting with gold, one becomes muddled.
The skill is the same in all cases,
but when one becomes self-important,
then one values external things.
In general, those who value external things are clumsy within."
Tián Kāizhī met with Duke Wēi of Zhōu.
Duke Wēi said,
"I have heard that Zhù Shèn has students.
You, sir, associate with Zhù Shèn,
what have you heard from him?"
Tián Kāizhī said,
"Kāizhī holds a broom and sweeps to attend to the doorway and courtyard,
how could I have heard anything from that master!"
Duke Wēi said,
"Master Tián, please do not decline,
I, your subject, wish to hear it."
Kāizhī said,
"I heard from that master who said,
'Those who are good at nurturing life
are like shepherds,
they watch those who lag behind
and whip them.'"
Duke Wēi said,
"What does this mean?"
Tián Kāizhī said,
"In Lǔ, there was Dān Bào,
No strange rooster dared to answer,
and instead ran away."
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 observed the Lǚliáng 呂梁 falls,
where the water plunged thirty *rèn*,
and the spray flowed for forty *lǐ*,
a place where soft-shelled turtles, alligators, fish, and turtles could not swim.
He saw a man swimming there,
and thought that he was suffering and wanted to die,
so he ordered his disciples to follow the current and rescue him.
He emerged after several hundred steps,
with disheveled hair, singing and walking along the bank below.
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 followed and asked him,
saying:
"I thought you were a ghost,
but observing you, you are a man.
May I ask,
is there a *dào* (way, principle) to treading water?"
He said:
"No,
I have no *dào*.
I begin with the familiar,
grow with my nature,
and complete it with fate.
I enter with the whirlpool,
and exit with the surging water,
following the *dào* of the water
without imposing myself upon it.
This is how I tread the water."
Confucius said:
"What does it mean to begin with what is inherent,
grow with one's nature,
and achieve through destiny?"
He said:
"I was born on a hill
and feel at ease on a hill,
this is inherent;
I grew up by the water
and feel at ease by the water,
this is my nature;
I do not know the reason why I am like this,
this is destiny."
Zǐ Qìng carved wood to make a *jù* (musical instrument stand),
when the *jù* was completed,
those who saw it were as astonished as if it were the work of ghosts or spirits.
The Marquis of Lǔ saw it and asked him,
saying:
"What technique do you use to make it?"
He replied, saying:
"I am a craftsman,
what technique do I have!
However, there is one thing.
When I am about to make a *jù*,
I never dare to expend my energy,
I must purify myself to calm my mind.
After purifying myself for three days,
I dare not think of celebrations, rewards, or noble ranks;
After fasting for five days,
one dares not harbor thoughts of praise, blame, skill, or clumsiness;
after fasting for seven days,
one abruptly forgets that one has limbs and a form.
At this time,
there is no court business;
the skill is focused
and external cleverness disappears;
then one enters the mountains and forests,
observes the natural disposition;
the form and substance are fully realized,
then one conceives of the *jù* (鐻) [a kind of bell stand],
then one puts hands to it;
otherwise, one stops.
Thus, using the natural to harmonize with the natural,
is this not the reason why the artifact causes doubt in the spirits!"
Dōngyě Jì (東野稷) was presented to Duke Zhuāng (莊公) for his chariot driving skills.
His advances and retreats were perfectly aligned with the plumb line,
his left and right turns were perfectly aligned with the compass.
Duke Zhuāng (莊公) thought his skill was beyond compare,
and had him hook one hundred times, then return.
Yán Hé (顏闔) encountered him [on the way back],
and went in to see the Duke, saying:
"Jì's (稷) horses are about to fail."
The Duke kept it secret and did not respond.
Shortly after,
they indeed failed and returned.
The Duke said:
“How do you know this?”
He replied,
“The horse’s strength is exhausted,
yet he still seeks to urge it on;
therefore, I say it will fail.”
When Gōng Chuí spun and covered the compass and square,
his finger transformed with the object
and he did not examine it with his mind;
therefore, his spiritual platform was unified and not fettered.
Forgetting the foot makes the shoe comfortable;
forgetting the waist makes the belt comfortable;
knowing to forget right and wrong
makes the mind comfortable;
not changing internally,
not following externally
makes dealing with events comfortable.
Beginning with comfort
and never not being comfortable,
is forgetting the comfort of comfort.
There was one Sūn Xiū who,
coming to the door, boasted to Zǐ Biǎn Qìngzǐ, saying:
“Living in the village, I am not considered uncultivated;
facing difficulty, I am not considered unwary;
however, the fields do not meet with good years,
serving the ruler does not meet with a good era;
a guest in the village,
pursued in the state,
In that case, what crime did Hú commit against Heaven?
Why did Xiū encounter this fate?"
Biǎn Zǐ said:
"Have you alone not heard
of the way the ultimate person conducts himself?
He forgets his liver and gall,
abandons his ears and eyes,
vaguely wanders beyond the dust and grime,
leisurely roams in the realm of effortless action.
This is called acting without relying,
nurturing without controlling.
Now, you adorn your wisdom to startle the foolish,
cultivate your person to illuminate the impure,
shining brightly as if carrying the sun and moon while walking.
You are fortunate to have a complete physical form,
with all nine orifices intact,
not dying prematurely crippled, deaf, or blind,
and being counted among humankind.
This is already a great fortune;
what time do you have to resent Heaven?
Be gone!"
Sūn Zǐ departed.
Biǎn Zǐ went inside,
sat for a while,
and looked up to the sky and sighed.
His disciple asked:
"Why is it that you sigh, Master?"
Biǎn Zǐ said:
"Those who previously left,
I will tell them about the virtue of the Perfected Person,
but I fear they will be startled and consequently fall into confusion."
A disciple said, "That is not so.
What Sūnzǐ (孫子) said, is it correct?
What you, Teacher, said, is it incorrect?
What is incorrect certainly cannot confuse what is correct.
What Sūnzǐ said, is it incorrect?
What you, Teacher, said, is it correct?
They certainly came already confused,
what further fault is there in that!"
Biǎn Zǐ (扁子) said, "That is not so.
In the past, there was a bird that perched in the suburbs of Lǔ (魯);
the ruler of Lǔ delighted in it,
and prepared a great sacrifice to feast it,
and played the Jiǔsháo (九韶) music to please it.
The bird then began to worry, become sorrowful, and look dizzy,
not daring to eat or drink.
This is called using one's own way to nourish a bird.
As for nourishing a bird in the way that is proper for a bird,
it should be allowed to roost in deep forests,
float on rivers and lakes,
and be fed with eels;
then it would be content on flat land.
Now, Xiū (休)
is an ignorant commoner with limited knowledge.
If I were to tell him about the virtue of the Perfected Person,
it would be like loading a mouse onto a carriage with horses,
The joyous little sparrow uses bells and drums.
How could it not be startled!"
Chapter 20: Mountain Trees
Zhuāng Zǐ was walking in the mountains
when he saw a large tree
with flourishing branches and leaves.
Woodcutters stopped beside it
but did not cut it down.
He asked the reason,
and they said,
"It is useless."
Zhuāng Zǐ said,
"This tree, because of its lack of timber value,
is able to live out its natural lifespan."
The master came out of the mountains
and stayed at the house of an old friend.
The old friend was pleased
and ordered a servant to kill a goose and cook it.
The servant asked,
"One of them can honk,
and the other cannot honk.
Which one shall I kill?"
The master said, "Kill the one that cannot honk."
The next day,
a disciple asked Zhuāng Zǐ,
"Yesterday, the tree in the mountains
was able to live out its natural lifespan because of its lack of timber value;
"Now, the master's goose,
died because it was useless.
Where will you go, sir?"
Zhuāng Zǐ smiled and said,
"Zhōu will dwell between usefulness and uselessness.
The space between usefulness and uselessness
resembles it but is not it,
therefore one cannot avoid being burdened.
But if one rides on virtue and floats freely, it is not like that.
Without praise or blame,
sometimes a dragon, sometimes a snake,
transforming with the times,
and never insisting on being fixed;
sometimes rising, sometimes falling,
taking harmony as the measure,
floating freely in the source of all things;
manipulating all things, but not being manipulated by things,
then how could one be burdened!
This is the principle of Shén Nóng and the Yellow Emperor.
As for the emotions of the myriad things
and the traditions of human relationships, it is not like that.
Union leads to separation,
completion leads to destruction;
integrity leads to frustration,
honor leads to criticism,
action leads to loss,
talent leads to plotting,
incompetence leads to deception.
How can one be certain of anything?
Alas!
Disciples, remember this,
it is only the realm of virtue!"
Yí Liáo of the southern market saw the Marquis of Lǔ,
and the Marquis of Lǔ had a worried expression.
Shì Nán Zǐ yuē: Shì Nán Zǐ said:
"Jūn yǒu yōu sè, hé yě?" "Your Lordship has a worried expression, why is that?"
Lǔ hóu yuē: The Marquis of Lǔ said:
"Wú xué xiānwáng zhī dào, "I study the ways of the former kings,
xiū xiān jūn zhī yè; cultivate the undertakings of my former lords;
wú jìng guǐ zūn xián, I revere ghosts and honor the worthy,
qīn ér xíng zhī, I personally carry them out,
wú xūyú lí jū; without a moment's separation;
rán bù miǎn yú huàn, yet I cannot avoid misfortune,
wú shì yǐ yōu." I am worried about this."
Shì Nán Zǐ yuē: Shì Nán Zǐ said:
"Jūn zhī chú huàn zhī shù qiǎn yǐ! "Your Lordship's method of eliminating misfortune is shallow!
Fú fēng hú wén bào, Now, the plump fox and the patterned leopard,
qī yú shānlín, dwell in the mountains and forests,
fú yú yánxué, hide in the caves,
jìng yě; this is stillness;
yè xíng zhòu jū, they travel at night and dwell during the day,
jiè yě; this is vigilance;
suī jī kě yǐnyuē, even though they are hungry and thirsty and living in obscurity,
yóu qiě xū shū yú jiānghú zhī shàng still they roam about on the rivers and lakes
ér qiú shí yān, to seek food,
dìng yě; this is steadfastness;
Yet still, you cannot avoid the troubles of being caught in nets and traps.
What crime is there in this?
It is your skin that is the cause of your calamity.
Now, is the state of Lǔ not merely your skin?
I wish that you would hollow out your form and discard your skin,
cleanse your heart and remove your desires,
and wander in the fields of no one.
To the south of Yuè, there is a settlement,
named the land of Jiàndé.
Its people are foolish and simple,
having few selfish desires and little greed;
they know how to work but do not know how to hoard,
they give without seeking repayment;
they do not know where righteousness is appropriate,
they do not know where ritual leads;
they act wildly and rashly,
yet they tread upon the great square (the Way);
their lives are joyful,
and their deaths are worthy of burial.
I wish that you would leave your state and abandon worldly customs,
and walk together with the Way."
The ruler said,
"That way is distant and dangerous,
and there are rivers and mountains,
I have no boat or cart,
what should I do?"
Shì Nánzǐ said,
"Do not be arrogant in form,
"[I] will not stay; I will take it to the lord's chariot."
The lord said, "That road is secluded and distant, and there are no people.
With whom shall I be neighbors? I have no provisions,
I have no food; how can I get there?"
Shì Nánzǐ said, "Reduce your expenses,
lessen your desires, and although you have no provisions, it will be enough.
Your Majesty, cross the river and float on the sea, gaze upon it and not see its shore,
the more you go forward, the less you know where it ends. Those who see you off all return from the shore;
Your Majesty, you are far from here! Therefore, having possessions is a burden,
seeing others having possessions is a worry. Therefore, Yáo did not possess anything,
nor did he see others possessing anything. I wish to remove Your Majesty's burden,
eliminate Your Majesty's worries, and wander alone with the Dao in the Land of Great Nothingness.
If you are crossing a river in a raft, and an empty boat comes and bumps into your boat,
even a narrow-minded person will not be angry;
If there is a person on top of it [something unstated],
then he calls out Zhāng Xī’s name.
If he calls once and is not heard,
and calls again and is not heard,
then if he calls a third time,
he will surely follow it with harsh words.
Earlier he was not angry,
but now he is angry;
earlier he was empty, but now he is full.
If a person can empty himself to wander in the world,
who can harm him!"
Běigōng Shē levied taxes for Wèi Línggōng
to make a bell,
and built a platform outside the city gate.
In three months
it was completed, from top to bottom.
Wángzǐ Qìngjì saw it and asked him,
saying:
"What kind of technique did you employ?"
Shē said:
"In a moment of leisure,
I dared not employ any technique.
I have heard that,
'Once it is carved and polished,
it returns to simplicity.'
Simple and unperceiving,
negligent and uncertain;
dense and dull,
It sees off those who depart
and welcomes those who arrive;
those who come are not prohibited,
those who leave are not stopped;
it complies with their strength,
follows their crooked support,
relies on their self-sufficiency.
Therefore, morning and evening, it collects taxes
without diminishing even a hair's breadth,
how much more would it take a large contribution!"
Kǒngzǐ was besieged between Chén and Cài,
and for seven days had no cooked food.
Tàigōng Rèn went to console him, saying:
"Are you near death?"
He said:
"Yes."
"Do you dislike death?"
He said:
"Yes."
Rèn said:
"I shall tell you the way to not die.
In the Eastern Sea, there is a bird
named Yìdài.
As a bird, it flutters and flaps,
seeming to have no ability;
it flies by relying on support,
it roosts by clinging to danger;
advancing, it dares not be at the front,
In retreat, he dares not be last;
in eating, he dares not be the first to taste,
he always takes what is left.
Therefore, his ranks are not diminished,
and outsiders ultimately cannot harm him,
thus he is spared from misfortune.
Straight trees are felled first,
sweet wells are exhausted first.
Your intention, I suspect, is to display knowledge to startle the foolish,
to cultivate yourself to highlight the filth [of others],
shining brightly like carrying the sun and moon while walking,
therefore, you cannot avoid [trouble].
In the past, I heard it said by a person of great accomplishment:
'He who boasts of himself has no merit,
he who achieves success declines,
he who establishes a name diminishes.'
Who can relinquish merit and fame
and return to the common people!
The Way flows on, but it is not evident; dwell
so as to gain conduct without placing reliance upon a name;
purely and consistently,
he is then comparable to a madman;
erasing traces and abandoning influence,
not acting for merit or fame;
therefore, he has no demands on others,
and others also have no demands on him.
The perfect person is not heard of,
what are you so delighted about?"
Kǒngzǐ said, "Excellent!"
He severed ties with his acquaintances,
abandoned his disciples,
and fled to the great marshes.
He wore coarse hemp clothing,
and ate acorns.
He entered among the beasts without disturbing their herds,
and entered among the birds without disrupting their flocks.
The birds and beasts did not dislike him,
how much less would men!
Kǒngzǐ asked Zǐsāng Yú, saying:
"I was twice driven out of Lǔ,
my trees were felled in Sòng,
my footprints were erased in Wèi,
I was impoverished in Shāngzhōu,
and besieged between Chén and Cài.
I have encountered these several misfortunes,
my close friends have become increasingly distant,
and my disciples have become increasingly scattered.
Why is this?"
Zǐsāng Yú said:
"Have you not heard
of the escaped man of Jiǎ?
Línhuí discarded a jade worth a thousand gold pieces,
and carried a newborn infant as he fled.
Someone asked:
'Was it for the infant's clothing?
The infant's clothing is meager.
Was it for the infant's burden?
The infant's burden is heavy.
Why did you discard a jade worth a thousand gold pieces,
and carry a newborn infant as you fled?'
Línhuí said:
'They are joined by profit,
this is united by natural affinity."
Those who are united by profit
will abandon each other when pressed by poverty, disaster, trouble, or harm;
they will abandon each other.
Those who are united by natural affinity
will support each other when pressed by poverty, disaster, trouble, or harm.
The difference between supporting each other and abandoning each other is vast.
Moreover, the friendship of gentlemen is as light as water,
the friendship of petty men is as sweet as liquor;
gentlemen are intimate through lightness,
petty men break off through sweetness.
Those who unite for no reason
will separate for no reason."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"I respectfully receive your instruction!"
He walked slowly and lingered, then returned,
abandoning study and discarding books.
The disciples did not restrain him,
and their love for him increased even more.
Another day,
Sāng Yú again said:
"When Shùn was about to die,
Zhēn Língyǔ said:
"You must be careful!
For form, nothing is better than following the circumstances;
for emotion, nothing is better than following one's natural disposition.
By following the circumstances, one does not become detached;
by following one's natural disposition, one does not become weary.
If one is not detached and not weary,
then one does not seek embellishment
to wait for the form to be completed;
if one does not seek embellishment
to wait for the form to be completed,
then one certainly does not depend on external things."
Zhuāng Zǐ wore coarse cloth clothes with patches,
straightened his broken shoe laces
and passed by the King of Wèi.
The King of Wèi said, "Why are you so worn out, sir?"
Zhuāng Zǐ said:
"I am poor,
not worn out.
A scholar who possesses morality and virtue
but cannot put it into practice,
that is being worn out.
Wearing tattered clothes and worn-out shoes,
that is being poor,
not worn out;
this is what is called not encountering the right time.
Has Your Majesty not seen a leaping monkey?
When it finds itself among nán, zǐ, yù, or zhāng trees,
Entangling its branches, the wáng (王) moves freely within them;
even Yì (羿) and Péng Méng (蓬蒙) could not get a clear view of it.
But when it finds itself among thorn trees, jujube trees, and thorny bushes,
it moves cautiously and glances sideways,
trembling and fearful.
It's not that its muscles and bones have suddenly become more rigid
and less flexible;
it's that the situation is unfavorable,
and it's not enough to display its abilities.
Now, being situated amidst a dim ruler and chaotic ministers,
and wanting to be without distress,
how can that be achieved?
This is like Bǐ Gān's (比干) fate of having his heart cut out!"
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) was in dire straits between Chén (陳) and Cài (蔡),
for seven days without cooked food.
Leaning on withered wood with his left hand,
and striking a withered branch with his right,
he sang the tune of the "Yán Shì" (焱氏) wind,
having the instruments but lacking the prescribed number,
having the sound but lacking the notes of the scale.
The sound of the wood and the human voice,
resonated deeply, touching the hearts of the people.
Yán Huí (顏回) stood upright with folded hands
and turned his eyes back to observe him.
Zhòngní (仲尼) feared that he would expand himself and create greatness,
or love himself and create sorrow,
and said:
"Huí (回),
It is easy not to suffer loss from Heaven;
it is difficult not to receive benefit from others.
There is no beginning that is not also an end;
man and Heaven are one.
Now, who are those who sing?"
Huí replied,
"May I ask about
'It is easy not to suffer loss from Heaven'?"
Zhòngní said,
"Hunger, thirst, cold, and heat,
being trapped in poverty and unable to move,
are the actions of Heaven;
they are the way Heaven vents its processes on things;
to say that one goes with them as they pass is what it means.
As a minister,
one dares not leave them.
If holding to the way of a minister is still like this,
then what about the way one treats Heaven?"
"What is meant by
'It is difficult not to receive benefit from others'?"
Zhòngní said,
"When one begins to be employed and reaches all four corners [of the land],
and rank and emolument come together without end,
then that which benefits things
is not actually for oneself;
my fate has something that lies outside of me.
The princely man does not become a robber,
the worthy man does not become a thief.
If I were to take it, what would be the reason?
Therefore it is said:
No bird is more discerning than the yì'ér (鷾鴯, a kind of bird),
where its eyes deem unsuitable to stay,
it doesn't even bother to look,
even if the fruit falls right there,
it abandons it and flees.
Such is its fear of people,
yet it sneaks into human spaces,
where the altars of the soil and grain are maintained."
"What is meant by
'without beginning and without end'?"
Zhòng Ní (仲尼, Confucius) said:
"Transforming all things
without knowing who causes their changes,
how can one know their end?
How can one know their beginning?
Simply rectify yourself and await them."
"What is meant by the unity of man and Heaven?"
Zhòng Ní (仲尼, Confucius) said:
"Having man is Heaven;
having Heaven is also Heaven.
That man cannot possess Heaven
is nature.
The sage peacefully embodies the passage
and ends!"
Zhuāng Zhōu (莊周) was wandering in the thickets of Diāolíng (雕陵),
and saw a strange magpie coming from the south,
Its wings were seven feet wide,
its eyes were a full inch in diameter.
It bumped against Zhōu's forehead
and gathered in the chestnut grove.
Zhuāng Zhōu said, "What bird is this?
Its wings are so large yet it doesn't fly away,
its eyes are so large yet it doesn't see?"
He hitched up his robe and strode forward quickly,
holding a pellet and waiting for it.
He saw a cicada,
just enjoying the shade
and forgetting itself;
a mantis was holding up its forelegs to strike at it,
seeing its gain and forgetting its form;
a strange magpie followed to benefit from it,
seeing the benefit and forgetting its true self.
Zhuāng Zhōu was startled and said,
"Alas!
Things are inherently interconnected,
two kinds of things summon each other!"
He threw away the pellet and ran back,
the gamekeeper chased and scolded him.
Zhuāng Zhōu went back inside,
and for three months he didn't go to court.
Lìn Qiě followed and asked him,
"Master, why have you been so long absent from court lately?"
Zhuāng Zhōu said,
"I was guarding my form
and forgetting oneself;
observing muddy water
but becoming lost in clear pools.
Moreover, I have heard the Master say:
"Enter their customs,
follow their customs."
Now, I wander in Diāolíng
and forget myself;
a strange magpie strikes my forehead.
I wander in the chestnut forest and forget the truth;
the forest ranger of the chestnut forest
considers me worthy of punishment.
This is why I do not attend court."
Yángzǐ of Sòng
stayed overnight at an inn.
The innkeeper had two concubines,
one of whom was beautiful,
and one of whom was ugly.
The ugly one was valued, and the beautiful one was scorned.
Yángzǐ asked the reason for this,
and the innkeeper's boy replied:
"The beautiful one considers herself beautiful,
and I do not recognize her beauty.
The ugly one considers herself ugly,
and I do not recognize her ugliness."
Yángzǐ said:
"Disciples, remember this!
Practice virtue and discard self-congratulatory behavior;
"Where could one go and not be loved!"
Tián Zǐfāng, Chapter Twenty-one
Tián Zǐfāng was attending a seat beside Wèi Wénhóu,
and repeatedly praised Xīgōng.
Wénhóu said,
"Is Xīgōng your teacher?"
Zǐfāng said, "No,
he is a neighbor from the village of Wúzé;
his words are often appropriate,
therefore Wúzé praises him."
Wénhóu said, "Then do you not have a teacher?"
Zǐfāng said, "I do."
Wénhóu said,
"Who is your teacher?"
Zǐfāng said, "Dōngguō Shùnzǐ."
Wénhóu said,
"Then why have you never praised this master?"
Zǐfāng said,
"His character is genuine,
he has a human appearance but is like Heaven, empty
on the surface but preserving truth within,
pure yet tolerant of things.
If things are without the Dao,
he uses a proper demeanor to enlighten them,
causing people's intentions to vanish.
How could Wúzé be worthy of praising him!"
Zǐfāng left,
Wén Hóu 文侯, seemingly despondent, remained silent all day.
He summoned the minister standing before him and said to him,
"How distant is
a ruler of complete virtue!
Initially, I considered the words of sages and the actions of benevolence and righteousness to be the ultimate.
Now, having heard of Zǐ Fāng's 子方 teacher,
my body feels disjointed and unwilling to move,
my mouth feels clamped shut and unwilling to speak.
What I have learned is truly just a clay figure!
Indeed, the state of Wèi 魏 is truly a burden to me!"
Wēn Bó Xuě Zǐ 温伯雪子 was traveling to Qí 齊,
and lodged in Lǔ 魯.
A man of Lǔ 魯 requested to see him.
Wēn Bó Xuě Zǐ 温伯雪子 said,
"No.
I have heard that the gentlemen of the Central States
are clear about ritual propriety
but shallow in understanding people's hearts.
I do not wish to see him."
When he arrived in Qí 齊,
he returned and again lodged in Lǔ 魯.
The same man again requested to see him.
Wēn Bó Xuě Zǐ 温伯雪子 said,
"When I went before, he was eager to see me;
now he is again eager to see me.
He must have some way to inspire me."
He went out and met the guest,
then returned inside and sighed.
Tomorrow I am to meet a guest,
and again he entered and sighed.
His servant said:
"Every time you see a guest,
you invariably enter and sigh,
why is that?"
He said:
"I have already told you:
'The gentlemen of Zhōngguó [China]
are well-versed in rites and righteousness
but ignorant of understanding people's hearts.'
Those who saw me in the past,
their advances and retreats were all according to fixed rules, all according to set squares,
their composure was like a dragon, like a tiger,
their admonitions to me were like a son's,
their guidance of me was like a father's,
that is why I sigh."
Zhòng Ní [Confucius] met him but said nothing.
Zǐ Lù asked:
"Our master has wanted to meet Wēn Bó Xuě Zǐ for a long time,
but having met him, you say nothing, why is that?"
Zhòng Ní said:
"For such a person,
a glance is enough for the Dao to be present,
there is no room for words."
Yán Yuān asked Zhòng Ní, saying:
"When you walk, I walk;
when you trot, I trot;
when you run, I run;
when you gallop away, leaving dust behind,
I, Huí, am left gaping far behind!"
Confucius said:
"Huí, what do you mean?"
He said:
"When the Master walked,
I also walked;
When the Master spoke,
I also spoke;
When the Master hurried,
I also hurried;
When the Master debated,
I also debated;
When the Master galloped, I also galloped.
When the Master spoke of the Dao, I also spoke of the Dao.
But when you ran with untrammeled speed, leaving the dust far behind,
and I was left gaping behind,
it was because the Master is believed without speaking,
comprehensive without comparing,
and without instruments, the people surge forward,
not knowing why it is so."
Zhòng Ní (仲尼) said: "Alas!
How can this not be examined!
Truly, the greatest sorrow is the death of the heart,
and the death of the body is secondary.
The sun rises in the east
and sets in the westernmost reaches,
all things emulate this pattern.
Those with eyes and feet
depend on it for their success;
when it rises, they exist,
when it sets, they perish.
All things are like this;
some depend on something to die,
and some depend on something to live.
Once I receive my form,
I do not transform but wait for the end,
mimicking things and moving,
day and night without pause,
yet I do not know where it ends.
Insensibly, my form is completed,
knowing fate,
I cannot foresee what lies ahead;
Qiū 丘 grieves at the passing of each day.
I have interacted with you, my arm, all my life,
and now I will lose it.
How can I not be saddened by this!
You are surely attached to that to which I am attached.
It has already reached its end,
and you seek it as if it still exists,
which is like looking for a horse in an empty marketplace.
I have forgotten you so completely,
and you have forgotten me so completely.
Nevertheless,
why should you worry about it!
Even if you forget the old me,
there is still something that will not be forgotten.”
Kǒngzǐ met Lǎodān.
Lǎodān had just bathed,
and was about to let his hair down to dry,
appearing apprehensive and almost inhuman.
Kǒngzǐ withdrew and waited for him.
After a little while, he met him and
said:
"Qiū is bewildered,
is this really true?
Just now, Teacher, your form was withered like dried wood,
like something abandoned,
standing alone, detached from people."
Lǎodān said:
"I was wandering in the beginning of things."
Kǒngzǐ said: "What do you mean?"
Lǎodān said:
"My mind was troubled and could not know,
my mouth was silent and could not speak.
I will try to describe it for you.
Utmost Yin is solemn and still,
Utmost Yang is bright and radiant;
the solemnity arises from Heaven,
Its magnificence originates from the earth;
when the two interact and harmonize,
then things are produced.
Something governs them,
yet its form is never seen.
Ebbing and flowing, filling and emptying,
one darkness, one brightness,
daily changing, monthly transforming,
daily it does something,
yet its accomplishment is unseen.
Life has a source in sprouting,
death has a place to return to,
beginning and end oppose each other endlessly,
yet no one knows where it ends.
If it is not this,
then who is its ancestor!"
Kǒngzǐ said, "May I ask Yóu about this?"
Lǎodān said:
"To obtain this is ultimate beauty and ultimate joy.
To obtain ultimate beauty and wander in ultimate joy
is called the ultimate person."
Kǒngzǐ said, "I wish to hear the method."
He said:
"Grass-eating beasts do not worry about changing their thickets;
water-born insects do not worry about changing their water.
They perform small changes without losing their great constancy.
Joy, anger, sorrow, and happiness do not enter their hearts.
Now, the world
That which is the one source of all things.
Attaining that one source and becoming one with it,
then the four limbs and hundred parts of the body will be like dust and dirt,
and life, death, beginning, and end will be like day and night,
and nothing will be able to disrupt them.
How much less the interventions of gain, loss, misfortune, and fortune!
Abandoning servitude is like abandoning mud and mire.
Knowing that one's own self is more valuable than servitude,
its value lies in my own self
and is not lost through change.
Moreover, the myriad transformations
have never had a beginning or an end.
Who then is sufficient to trouble the mind?
One who has attained the Dao understands this."
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 said,
"The Master's virtue matches Heaven and Earth,
and yet he still relies on profound words to cultivate his mind.
Which of the gentlemen of antiquity
could escape this?"
Lǎodān 老聃 said, "Not so.
Water, when still,
acts without effort, and its talent is naturally revealed.
The perfect person's virtue
requires no cultivation,
yet things cannot leave them.
It is like Heaven being naturally high,
Earth being naturally thick,
and the sun and moon being naturally bright.
What should I cultivate!"
Kǒngzǐ exited
and told Yán Huí,
"My understanding of the Dao
is like that of a vinegar fly!
If not for the Master's uncovering me,
I would not know the entirety of Heaven and Earth."
Zhuāngzǐ met with Duke Āi of Lǔ.
Duke Āi said,
"Lǔ has many Confucian scholars,
but few who practice the Master's way."
Zhuāngzǐ said, "Lǔ has few Confucians."
Duke Āi said, "The entire state of Lǔ wears Confucian garb,
how can you say there are few?"
Zhuāngzǐ said, "I have heard that
Confucianists who wear round caps
know the seasons of Heaven;
those who wear square shoes
know the lay of the land;
and those who wear jade pendants at their waist
are decisive when matters arise.
A gentleman who possesses the Dao
does not necessarily wear its clothing;
one who wears its clothing
does not necessarily know the Dao.
If you, sir, believe otherwise,
why not announce throughout the state:
'Those who wear this clothing without this Dao
"His crime deserves death!"'
Thereupon, Āi Gōng mourned for him for five days,
and in the state of Lǔ no one dared to wear Confucian garb.
There was only one man who, wearing Confucian garb,
stood at the palace gate.
The duke immediately summoned him and questioned him about affairs of state.
He answered a thousand times, ten thousand ways, yet was never exhausted.
Zhuāngzǐ said:
"Considering the state of Lǔ, is one Confucian really many?"
Can that be considered a lot?
Bǎilǐ Xī's concern for emolument and rank did not enter his mind,
therefore he fed the oxen and they grew fat,
causing Duke Mù of Qín to forget his lowly status
and entrust him with the government.
Yǒu Yú Shì's concern for
life and death did not enter his mind,
therefore he was able to move people.
Lord Yuán of Sòng was about to commission a painting,
and all the scribes arrived,
accepting greetings
and standing at attention.
Licking their brushes and mixing ink,
half of them were doing it outside.
There was one scribe who arrived late,
leisurely and not hurrying,
accepting greetings but not standing,
and went directly to his lodging.
The duke sent someone to observe him,
Then he untied his clothes and
sat cross-legged, naked.
The ruler said:
"Acceptable,
this is a true painter!"
Wén Wáng 文王 observed at Zāng 臧 and
saw a man fishing,
but his fishing seemed not to be fishing;
it wasn't that he held his fishing rod
to fish,
but he was always fishing.
Wén Wáng 文王 wanted to appoint
him and entrust him with the government,
but he feared that the ministers and elder brothers would not be at ease;
he wanted to leave it at that and release him,
but he couldn't bear that the common people would be without a "heaven".
Therefore, at dawn, he addressed the officers, saying:
"In the past, I, your ruler, dreamt of a good man,
black-skinned and bearded,
riding a piebald horse with one red hoof,
who proclaimed:
'Entrust your government to the old man of Zāng 臧,
perhaps the people will have some relief!'"
The gentlemen suddenly said:
"The former ruler commanded the King!"
Wén Wáng 文王 said: "In that case, let us divine it."
The gentlemen said: "The command of the former ruler,
the King should have no other choice,
Why then would he divine!"
He then welcomed Zāng Zhàngrén
and entrusted him with the government.
The established laws were not changed,
and biased orders did not originate.
After three years,
King Wén looked upon his state,
and saw the officials cultivating diligently
and organizing into groups.
Those in positions of authority did not fail to cultivate virtue,
and the measures of quantity and capacity dared not be falsified within the borders.
The officials cultivated diligently
and organized into groups,
which meant they respected unity of purpose;
those in positions of authority did not fail to cultivate virtue,
which meant they shared their duties;
the measures of quantity and capacity dared not be falsified within the borders,
which meant the feudal lords had no divided loyalties.
King Wén therefore regarded him as a great teacher,
faced north, and asked:
"Can the government be extended to encompass all under Heaven?"
Zāng Zhàngrén remained silent and did not respond,
but vaguely offered his resignation,
taking leave in the morning and fleeing by night,
never to be heard from again.
Yán Yuān asked Zhòngní:
"Was King Wén still unsure?
"Then why do you dream about it?"
Zhòng Ní said, "Silence,
you must not speak!
King Wén has exhausted it,
and what further criticism can there be!
He merely followed this a little while."
Liè Yǔkòu demonstrated archery for Bó Hūn Wú Rén.
He drew the bow fully,
placed a cup of water on his elbow,
and released the arrow.
The successive arrows arrived swiftly,
and the next arrow was already in place.
At that time, he was like a wooden figure.
Bó Hūn Wú Rén said,
"This is archery as archery,
not archery as non-archery.
Let me try ascending a high mountain with you,
treading on precarious rocks,
overlooking a hundred-ren abyss.
Can you still shoot then?"
Thereupon, Wú Rén ascended a high mountain,
trod on precarious rocks,
and overlooked a hundred-ren abyss.
He backed away slowly,
with two-fifths of his feet hanging outwards.
He greeted Yǔkòu and urged him forward.
Yǔkòu prostrated himself on the ground,
sweat flowing to his heels.
Bó Hūn Wú Rén said:
"The ultimate person
above peers into the azure sky,
below dives into the yellow springs,
extends and spreads to the eight limits,
yet their spirit and qi do not change.
Now, you are startled and have the aspiration to stare intently.
You are in danger in your heart!"
Jiān Wú asked Sūn Shū'áo, saying:
"You were three times appointed as Prime Minister
yet did not seek glory or splendor,
and three times resigned
without a worried expression.
I initially doubted you,
but now I see the space between your eyebrows is carefree and content.
What is your unique approach to managing your mind?"
Sūn Shū'áo said:
"How am I superior to others?
I consider its coming unavoidable,
and its departure unstoppable.
I consider gain and loss not to be about me,
and therefore I have no worried expression, that's all.
How am I superior to others?
Moreover, I do not know whether it resides there
or resides in me.
If it resides there,
then I am lost;
if it resides in me,
Let's get away from there.
While they are still hesitating,
still looking around,
how could they have time to reach the point of valuing some people and despising others!"
Zhòng Ní heard this and said,
"The truly perfect people of ancient times,
the wise could not persuade them,
beauties could not seduce them,
robbers could not plunder them,
Fú Xī and the Yellow Emperor could not befriend them.
Life and death are also great matters,
but they do not change them,
how much less would rank and emolument!
If one is like that,
then their spirit passes through great mountains without obstruction,
enters into deep springs without getting wet,
dwells in low and insignificant places without getting weary,
fills the universe
without being deficient, and having already given to others,
one has more oneself."
The King of Chǔ was sitting with the ruler of Fán,
after a short while,
the attendants of the King of Chǔ said,
"Fán has perished three times."
The ruler of Fán said,
"The perishing of Fán
is not enough to diminish my existence.
If 'the perishing of Fán is not enough to diminish my existence,'
then the existence of Chǔ is not sufficient to preserve existence.
Viewing it from this perspective,
then everything has never begun to perish,
and Chǔ has never begun to exist."
Chapter 22: Zhī Běi Yóu (Knowledge Wanders North)
Zhī Běi (Knowledge of the North) wandered above the Dark Water,
ascended the hill of Yǐn Fèn,
and happened to encounter Wú Wéi Wèi there.
Zhī said to Wú Wéi Wèi:
"I wish to ask you:
What thinking and what pondering will lead to knowing the Dao?
What dwelling and what clothing will bring peace in the Dao?
What following and what path will lead to attaining the Dao?"
He asked three times, but Wú Wéi Wèi did not answer.
It wasn't that he didn't want to answer,
but that he didn't know how to answer.
Zhī couldn't get an answer,
so he returned to the south of the White Water,
ascended the hill of Hú Quē,
and saw Kuáng Qū there.
Zhī used those words to ask Kuáng Qū.
Kuáng Qū said:
"Alas!
I know it,
I am about to tell you."
He was about to speak
but forgot what he wanted to say.
Having realized that he could gain no information by asking,
he returned to the imperial palace,
and saw the Yellow Emperor and asked him about it.
The Yellow Emperor said:
"Without thinking, without pondering,
one begins to know the Dao;
without dwelling, without adhering,
one begins to be at peace with the Dao;
without following, without guiding,
one begins to obtain the Dao."
Zhī asked the Huángdì, saying:
"I and you know it,
they and those do not know it,
which one is right?"
The Huángdì said:
"They are without effort, saying it is truly so;
the mad and twisted are like this;
I and you will never be close.
For those who know do not speak,
those who speak do not know;
therefore, the sage practices the teaching of non-speaking.
The Dao cannot be attained,
Virtue cannot be reached.
Benevolence can be fabricated,
Righteousness can be diminished,
Ritual is mutual falsehood.
Therefore, it is said:
'Having lost the Dao, then comes Virtue;
Losing Dé (德) comes before having Rén (仁);
losing Rén (仁) comes before having Yì (義);
losing Yì (義) comes before having Lǐ (禮).
Lǐ (禮),
is the flower of the Dao (道) and the beginning of chaos."
Therefore, it is said:
"Those who pursue the Dao (道) diminish day by day;
diminishing and diminishing again,
until they arrive at wúwéi (無為),
wúwéi (無為)
and yet there is nothing that is not done."
Now that it has already become a thing,
to desire to return to the root,
is it not difficult?
That which is easy, it is only the great person who can do it!
Life is a companion of death;
death is the beginning of life.
Who knows their order?
Human life is the gathering of qì (氣);
gathering becomes life,
scattering becomes death.
If death and life are companions,
what do I have to worry about?
Therefore, all things are one;
that which they deem beautiful becomes marvelous,
that which they detest becomes foul and rotten.
Foul and rotten things transform back into marvelous things;
marvelous things transform back into foul and rotten things.
Therefore, it is said:
"All under Heaven is connected by a single breath."
The sage values the One.
Zhì said to Huángdì:
"I asked Wúwéiwèi,
but Wúwéiwèi did not answer me.
It's not that he didn't want to answer me,
but that he didn't know how to answer me.
I asked Kuáng Qū,
and Kuáng Qū wanted to tell me
but didn't tell me.
It's not that he didn't want to tell me,
but that in the middle of wanting to tell me,
he forgot.
Now I ask you,
and you know it, so why not be forthcoming?"
Huángdì said:
"He is genuine
because of his ignorance.
This one is similar
because of his forgetfulness.
You and I will ultimately not be forthcoming
because of our knowledge."
Kuáng Qū heard this
and considered Huángdì to have spoken wisely.
Heaven and Earth possess great beauty but do not speak of it;
the four seasons have clear laws but do not debate them;
All things have inherent principles but do not speak of them.
The sage, comprehending the beauty of Heaven and Earth
and mastering the principles of all things,
therefore the perfect man does nothing,
the great sage does not create,
but observes Heaven and Earth.
Now, that spiritual brilliance, most refined,
with its myriad transformations,
things already dead and alive,
square and round,
none know their root.
Spread out flat, and all things have existed firmly since ancient times.
The Six Directions are vast,
yet have not departed from within it;
the tip of an autumn hair is small,
yet awaits it to become a complete form.
All under Heaven sink and float,
never changing throughout their lives;
Yīn and Yáng, the Four Seasons, cycle and move,
each obtaining its order.
Confused as if lost yet existing,
flowing and shapeless yet divine,
all things are nurtured without knowing.
This is called the root and origin,
and can be observed in Heaven.
Niè Quē asked the Way of Bèi Yī.
Bèi Yī said:
"If you correct your form,
unify your vision,
heavenly harmony will arrive;
restrain your knowledge,
unify your measures,
the spirit will come to reside [in you].
Virtue will become your beauty,
the Dao will become your dwelling.
Your pupils will be like a newborn calf,
without seeking its cause!"
Before he finished speaking,
Niè Quē fell asleep.
Bèi Yī was greatly pleased,
and went away singing,
saying:
"His form is like withered bones,
his heart like dead ashes.
Truly he knows reality,
and does not cling to himself because of knowledge.
Dim and obscure,
without a mind, and cannot be consulted with.
What kind of person is he!"
Shùn asked Chéng, saying:
"Can the Dao be obtained and possessed?"
Chéng said:
"Your body is not yours to possess,
how could you possess the Dao?"
Shùn said:
"My body is not mine;
to whom does it belong?"
He said:
"It is the form entrusted by Heaven and Earth.
Life is not yours;
it is the harmony entrusted by Heaven and Earth.
Nature and destiny are not yours;
they are the obedience entrusted by Heaven and Earth.
Grandchildren are not yours;
they are the molting entrusted by Heaven and Earth.
Therefore, in walking, one does not know where one is going;
in dwelling, one does not know what one is holding onto;
in eating, one does not know what one tastes.
Heaven and Earth are the strong *yáng qì*;
how can one possibly possess them?"
Kǒngzǐ asked Lǎodān,
"Today I am free and at leisure;
may I venture to ask about the ultimate Dao?"
Lǎodān said:
"You must fast and purify yourself,
clear your mind,
cleanse your spirit,
and discard your knowledge!
The Dao
is so obscure and difficult to speak of!
I will speak to you of its general outline.
Brightness is born from darkness,
order is born from formlessness,
Spirit is born from the Dao;
form is fundamentally born from essence.
And all things are produced from form.
Therefore, creatures with nine orifices are born from wombs;
creatures with eight orifices are born from eggs.
Its coming leaves no trace,
its going has no limit.
It has no door, no room;
it is the vast expanse that reaches in all directions.
Those who embrace this [Dao],
their limbs are strong,
their thoughts are truly clear,
their ears and eyes are sharp,
their minds exert no effort,
and their response to things is without fixed method.
Heaven cannot but be high,
Earth cannot but be broad,
the sun and moon cannot but move,
and the myriad things cannot but flourish.
This is its Dao!
"Moreover, 'extensive knowledge does not necessarily mean wisdom,
and eloquent debate does not necessarily mean intelligence,'
the sages have already made this clear.
As for that which is increased without any increase,
and diminished without any diminution,
this is what the sages preserve.
It is deep, like the sea;
it is majestic, its end is but a return to its beginning;
It carries and supports all things without depletion.
Then the way of the superior man
—that is its external aspect!
All things go to draw from it without it being depleted,
this is its way!
“There is a person in the Central Kingdom (Zhōngguó),
neither *yīn* nor *yáng*,
dwelling in the space between Heaven and Earth,
upright and acting as a person,
who will return to the origin.
Viewing it from the root,
life is but a gathering of muffled, fermenting things.
Though there be long life and short life,
how much difference is there?
A matter of a moment's speech.
How could this suffice to judge the rights and wrongs of Yáo and Jié!
Fruits and melons have their order,
human relationships, though difficult,
are the means by which they are ranked.
The sage meets with them and does not defy them,
passes them by and does not cling to them.
He tunes himself and responds to them,
this is virtue (dé);
accidentally he responds to them,
this is the Way (dào);
it is that from which the Emperors arise,
and the Kings originate.
"Life between Heaven and Earth,
is like a white colt glimpsed through a crack,
vanishing in an instant.
Suddenly and abruptly,
nothing fails to emerge from it;
smoothly and quietly,
nothing fails to enter into it.
Having transformed to be born,
it transforms again to die.
Creatures grieve for it,
humankind mourns for it.
Untying its celestial coverings,
dropping its celestial wrappings,
in confusion and distress,
the soul and spirit are about to depart,
and the body follows them,
returning to the Great Return!
The form of the formless,
the formless of the form,
is what all people commonly know,
but is not what the coming perfection attends to;
this is what the masses commonly discuss.
But perfection does not discuss,
and if it discusses, it is not perfection.
Clear vision is without value,
debate is not as good as silence.
The Dao cannot be heard,
hearing is not as good as blocking.
This is called a great attainment."
Dōngguō Zǐ asked Zhuāng Zǐ,
"This so-called Dào,
where does it exist?"
Zhuāng Zǐ said,
"It is nowhere that it does not exist."
Dōngguō Zǐ said, "Specify it further."
Zhuāng Zǐ said,
"It is in the ant."
He said,
"How could it be so low?"
He said,
"It is in the panic grass."
He said,
"How could it be even lower?"
He said,
"It is in the tiles and bricks."
He said,
"How could it be even more extreme?"
He said,
"It is in the excrement and urine."
Dōngguō Zǐ did not reply.
Zhuāng Zǐ said,
"Your question, Master,
fundamentally does not get to the substance.
Zhèng Huò's question to the market overseer about treading on a pig,
the further down it goes, the more accurate it becomes.
You must not insist on a particular place;
There is nowhere to escape things.
The supreme Dao is like this;
Great words are also like this.
"周" (zhōu - encompassing), "徧" (biàn - universal), and "咸" (xián - all) these three,
Have different names but the same reality;
Their meaning is one.
Once, we wandered together in the palace of "无何有" (wú hé yǒu - Nothingness),
Uniting and discussing,
Without ever reaching a final conclusion!
Once, we practiced non-action together!
Tranquil and peaceful!
Serene and clear!
Harmonious and leisurely!
My will is free and empty,
Going nowhere, yet I know not where it will arrive.
Departing and returning, not knowing where to stop,
I have already traveled to and fro,
And do not know where it will end.
Wandering about in the vast expanse,
Great knowledge enters therein,
Yet I know not where it ends.
That which "things" things has no boundary with "things,"
But "things" that are "thinged" have boundaries;
That which is called the boundary of things,
Is the boundary of no boundary,
Or the no-boundary of boundary.
Calling it fullness, emptiness, decline, and death,
That which is called fullness and emptiness is not fullness and emptiness;
"That which is considered decay and death is not decay and death;
that which is considered root and branch is not root and branch;
that which is considered accumulation and dispersal is not accumulation and dispersal."
Ē Hè Gān and Shén Nóng
studied together under Lǎo Lóng Jí.
Shén Nóng leaned on his armrest, closed the door, and stayed in darkness day and night.
Ē Hè Gān opened the door wide at midday
and entered, saying:
"Lǎo Lóng is dead!"
Shén Nóng leaned on his armrest, grasped his staff and rose.
He threw down his staff with a bang and laughed,
saying:
"Heaven knows my stubbornness, rudeness, and boasting,
therefore it has abandoned me and died.
Alas, Master!
He has died without anyone to unleash my wild words upon!"
Yǎn Gāng Diào heard of this
and said:
"Those who embody the Dao
are to whom the gentlemen of the world are attached.
Now, regarding the Dao,
they have not obtained even one ten-thousandth of the tip of an autumn hair,
and yet they still knew to conceal their wild words before dying.
How much more so should those who truly embody the Dao!
It is invisible to the eye,
inaudible to the ear,
and in the estimation of people,
To speak of it as "mingming" (冥冥, obscure),
is to discuss the Dao, but it is not the Dao itself."
Thereupon, Tàiqīng (泰清) asked Wúqióng (无穷),
"Do you know the Dao?"
Wúqióng (无穷) said, "I do not know."
He further asked Wúwéi (无为).
Wúwéi (无为) said,
"I know the Dao."
He said,
"Your knowledge of the Dao,
does it also have numerical limitations?"
He said,
"It does."
He said,
"What are its numerical limitations like?"
Wúwéi (无为) said,
"I know that the Dao can be honored,
can be despised,
can be contracted,
can be dispersed.
This is how I know the numerical limitations of the Dao."
Tàiqīng (泰清), based on what he said,
asked Wúshǐ (无始),
"If that is so,
then, Wúqióng's (无穷) not knowing and Wúwéi's (无为) knowing,
which is right and which is wrong?"
Wúshǐ (无始) said,
"Not knowing is deep,
Knowing it is shallow;
not knowing is internal;
knowing is external."
Thereupon, in the midst of the Great Clarity (Tài Qīng), he sighed and said:
"Not knowing is knowing!
Knowing is not knowing!
Who knows the knowledge of not knowing,
the knowing of not knowing?" Wúshǐ said:
"The Dao cannot be heard;
what is heard is not it;
the Dao cannot be seen;
what is seen is not it;
the Dao cannot be spoken;
what is spoken is not it.
Know the form of the formless!
The Dao does not fit a name."
Wúshǐ said:
"One who responds to questions about the Dao
does not know the Dao.
Even the one asking about the Dao
has not heard the Dao.
The Dao is without questions;
questions are without answers.
To question the questionless
is to exhaust the question;
to answer the answerless
is to be without interiority.
To await the exhausted question with no interiority,
Such a person,
outwardly does not observe the universe,
inwardly does not understand the Great Beginning.
Therefore, he does not cross over Kūnlún
nor roam in the Great Void."
Guāng Yào asked Wúyǒu,
"Does the master exist?
Or does he not exist?"
Wúyǒu did not answer him. Guāng Yào could not question him and carefully observed his appearance.
He was deep and empty.
Observing him all day long, he could not be seen;
listening to him, he could not be heard;
grasping at him, he could not be attained.
Guāng Yào said,
"He has reached the ultimate!
Who can reach this state?
I can have nothing,
but I cannot have nothing of nothing.
Even if I become nothing,
how can I reach this state!"
